lesson.title: Arccot: Completing the Trio
lesson.summary: The derivative of arccot x is -1/(1+x^2), the mirror image of arctan's derivative, completing the derivative toolkit for all six inverse trig functions.
lesson.body:
Cotangent, like tangent, has no gap to work around, so arccot x can be defined on all of the real line. The standard calculus convention restricts cotangent to the open interval (0, pi), where it decreases steadily from positive infinity down to negative infinity, so arccot x has domain all real numbers and range (0, pi), passing through pi/2 at x = 0. It is worth flagging that a few other fields use a different range convention for arccot, so it is always worth confirming which one a formula assumes before trusting it; the (0, pi) convention is the one that matches the derivative formula used throughout this course.

That range choice makes a shortcut available, the same kind used for arccos. Let theta = arctan x, so theta is in (-pi/2, pi/2) and tan theta = x. The cofunction identity cot(pi/2 - theta) = tan theta then says pi/2 - theta is exactly the angle in (0, pi) with cotangent equal to x, which by definition is arccot x. So arctan x + arccot x = pi/2 for every real x. Differentiating both sides, the constant pi/2 disappears, leaving d/dx[arccot x] = -d/dx[arctan x] = -1/(1+x^2).

The same result also falls out of implicit differentiation directly, which is worth doing once for full rigor. Let y = arccot x, so cot y = x. Differentiating implicitly gives -csc^2 y times y' = 1, so y' = -1/csc^2 y. The identity csc^2 y = 1 + cot^2 y = 1 + x^2 holds regardless of which quadrant y is in, since csc^2 y is always positive, so no absolute value is needed here, just as with arctan. Substituting gives d/dx[arccot x] = -1/(1+x^2).

For practice, differentiate y = arccot(x/3). With u = x/3 and u' = 1/3, the chain rule gives dy/dx = -u'/(1+u^2) = -(1/3)/(1 + x^2/9) = -(1/3) times 9/(9+x^2) = -3/(9+x^2). At x = 0, this gives -1/3, a negative slope, consistent with arccot being a decreasing function everywhere.
